metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with deployable JAX-WS entry point and Oracle database backend. Single-service application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Service owns persistent state (Oracle DB with INSERT operations) and exposes a write endpoint (submitOrder). No multi-service orchestration or event consumption patterns.

findings.title: No modern API interface — SOAP-only endpoint
findings.description: The service exposes a SOAP 1.1 RPC/encoded endpoint via JAX-WS. The WSDL is hand-maintained and drifts from implementation. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Modern agent frameworks cannot bind to SOAP natively.
findings.gap: No REST or modern API interface. SOAP RPC/encoded is deprecated. Agent tool frameworks cannot consume WSDL/SOAP natively.
findings.recommendation: Expose submitOrder as a REST POST endpoint with JSON request/response. Generate OpenAPI spec. Deprecate SOAP endpoint.

findings.title: No machine identity authentication
findings.description: No authentication mechanism exists in the source code. README mentions WS-Security but no implementation is committed. Any caller with network access can invoke the endpoint without authentication.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. No principal attribution. Service is completely unauthenticated.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials flow or API key authentication with distinct agent identities and principal attribution in audit logs.

findings.title: Write operations are not idempotent
findings.description: The submitOrder operation performs an unconditional INSERT with no idempotency key, no duplicate detection, and no unique constraint. Duplicate submissions create duplicate records.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism. No unique constraints on business keys. Retry creates duplicates.
findings.recommendation: Add UNIQUE constraint on (partner_id, po_number) and implement idempotency key support in the API contract.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no idempotency mechanism
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: submitOrder performs unconditional INSERT with no duplicate detection — agent retries will create duplicate orders.

findings.title: No compensation or rollback for write operations
findings.description: The submitOrder operation performs a single INSERT with no transaction management, no rollback capability, and no compensation logic. Submitted orders cannot be reversed programmatically.
findings.gap: No compensation or rollback. No cancel/void endpoint. No transaction management.
findings.recommendation: Add database transaction management and a cancelOrder endpoint. Implement saga-pattern compensation with status-based order lifecycle.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no rollback mechanism
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Write-enabled agents executing multi-step workflows cannot reverse failed operations — submitted orders are permanently committed.

findings.title: No audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No logging of any kind exists. No logging framework imported. Write operations leave no trace of who performed them. Complete absence of audit capability.
findings.gap: Zero audit logging. No logging framework. Impossible to identify who performed what action.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging with caller identity on every write. Deploy to immutable store (CloudWatch with retention or S3 with Object Lock).

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no audit logging
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Write-enabled agents must have full audit attribution. No logging exists at all — cannot prove compliance or conduct forensics.

findings.title: No scoped permissions — all callers have unlimited access
findings.description: No authorization model exists. No IAM policies, no role definitions, no permission checks. Any caller has full access to all operations with no mechanism to scope down.
findings.gap: Cannot scope agent permissions. No differentiation between callers.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway with IAM authorization policies supporting per-caller scoping.

compensating_controls: API Gateway with IAM-based authorization and scoped policies per caller
Network-level access control to limit which agents can reach the service

findings.title: No action-level authorization
findings.description: Single write operation with no mechanism to allow read-only access. No RBAC, ABAC, or permission matrix exists.
findings.gap: Cannot differentiate read vs write access per caller identity.
findings.recommendation: Add separate read endpoints with distinct authorization requirements enforced at gateway or application layer.

compensating_controls: API Gateway method-level authorization
Proxy layer that blocks unauthorized operations

findings.title: Credentials hardcoded in source code
findings.description: Database credentials are hardcoded in plaintext: DB_USER='partner_app', DB_PASS='partner2009'. Committed to git with no secrets management or rotation.
findings.gap: Credentials in source code. No rotation. Exposed in git history.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation. Rotate the exposed password immediately.

compensating_controls: Rotate compromised credentials immediately
Restrict database network access

findings.title: Cannot suspend individual agent identities
findings.description: No identity management exists. No mechanism to suspend or revoke individual agent access without taking down the service.
findings.gap: No identity lifecycle management. Cannot isolate misbehaving agents.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key management with revocation capability per agent identity.

compensating_controls: Network-level IP blocking
API Gateway with API key revocation

findings.title: No rate limiting or throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application throttling. Runaway agent loop would hit Oracle directly without protection.
findings.gap: No protection against traffic storms from runaway agents.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with throttling configuration before agent integration.

compensating_controls: API Gateway with usage plans and throttling
WAF rate rules

findings.title: No transaction limits on agent operations
findings.description: No transaction limits exist. No cap on orders per session, per hour, or per caller. An agent error could submit thousands of purchase orders.
findings.gap: No business-domain limits on agent operations. Unbounded write capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller order submission limits at the application or gateway layer.

compensating_controls: API Gateway usage plan with daily/monthly quota
Application-level counter per partner per time window

findings.title: No access control differentiation for data access
findings.description: Stage A: System stores partner-specific data (partner IDs, PO numbers, amounts). B1: CLEAR — response is a simple string. B2: FIRES — no access control differentiation, all callers get identical access. B3: No formal classification (INFO).
findings.gap: No access control differentiation. Raw exception messages may leak internal details.
findings.recommendation: Implement access control differentiation. Sanitize error responses to exclude internal details.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: B2 fires (no access control differentiation), B1 CLEAR (response is not structured payload with sensitive fields)
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 B2 fired because all callers receive identical responses with no scope differentiation. B1 CLEAR because response format is a simple string, not a structured data payload with sensitive fields to exclude.

b1.reasoning: Response is a simple string (ACCEPTED/ERROR), not a structured data payload with sensitive fields to exclude.

b2.reasoning: No access control differentiation exists. All callers have identical access with no mechanism to scope.

b3.reasoning: No formal data classification metadata exists.

findings.title: Data residency requirements undefined
findings.description: Data stored at hardcoded internal IP with no residency documentation. No region constraints, no sovereignty documentation. Compliance posture for cross-border data transmission is undefined.
findings.gap: No data residency documentation or controls. Compliance posture unknown.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements. Implement region controls if partners are in regulated jurisdictions.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=write-enabled but no explicit regulated data indicators (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI) found
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Write-enabled scope would normally resolve to BLOCKER, but no explicit regulated data indicators are present — partner order data without documented PII classification. Evaluated as RISK-SAFETY.

findings.title: No PII redaction capability — error messages leak internal details
findings.description: No logging framework exists. Error messages return raw exception text to callers including potential connection strings and credentials. When logging is added, PII redaction must be built in from day one.
findings.gap: No logging exists. When added, PII redaction needed. Error responses currently leak internal info.
findings.recommendation: Implement PII redaction in logging pipeline from the start. Sanitize error responses immediately.

compensating_controls: Structured logging with field-level redaction
Sanitize exception messages immediately

findings.title: No draft/pending state for agent-proposed writes
findings.description: submitOrder immediately commits to database. No two-step create-then-confirm pattern, no status field, no approval workflow. All writes are immediately committed.
findings.gap: No reviewable intermediate state for agent-proposed actions.
findings.recommendation: Add order status lifecycle (PENDING → CONFIRMED) with separate confirmation endpoint.

compensating_controls: Agent-side confirmation flow before calling submitOrder
PENDING status with separate confirm endpoint

findings.title: No configurable approval gates
findings.description: No approval gates. No configurable operation-level flags. All operations execute immediately without human approval option.
findings.gap: Cannot require human approval for high-risk agent operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement configurable approval gates — orders above threshold require human confirmation.

compensating_controls: Agent orchestration layer approval gate
Manual review for orders above threshold

findings.title: Machine-readable spec is outdated and unreliable
findings.description: WSDL exists but uses deprecated RPC/encoded style, is hand-maintained, and drifts from implementation. No OpenAPI or modern spec.
findings.gap: No reliable modern machine-readable spec. WSDL is deprecated and inaccurate.
findings.recommendation: Generate OpenAPI spec from REST endpoint code annotations after API modernization.

findings.title: Unstructured error responses
findings.description: Errors returned as 'ERROR:' + raw exception message. No structured error format, no error codes, no retryable classification.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable vs terminal errors. Raw exception messages exposed.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured error responses with error codes and retryable indicators.

findings.title: Write-only interface — cannot query current state
findings.description: No read/query endpoints. Only submitOrder (write). Agent cannot inspect state before acting.
findings.gap: Agent cannot read state before deciding next steps.
findings.recommendation: Add getOrder and listOrders query endpoints.

findings.title: No circuit breakers or resilience patterns
findings.description: Raw JDBC connection with no timeout, no retry logic, no circuit breaker. Database failures cascade directly to callers.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns. No circuit breakers. No timeouts.
findings.recommendation: Add JDBC timeouts, circuit breaker pattern, and retry policies for transient failures.

compensating_controls: JDBC connection timeout
API Gateway integration timeout

findings.title: Zero input validation — XXE and SQL injection vulnerabilities
findings.description: No input validation. XML parsed without XXE protection. Values concatenated into SQL (injection). No schema enforcement. No structured validation errors.
findings.gap: Accepts arbitrary input. Multiple injection vulnerabilities. No validation error responses.
findings.recommendation: Add XXE protection, parameterized queries (PreparedStatement), input validation, and structured error responses.

findings.title: No API versioning or breaking change detection
findings.description: WSDL is hand-maintained with no versioning, no changelog, no breaking change detection. Spec drifts from implementation.
findings.gap: No versioning. No breaking change detection. Agent tool bindings break silently.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning and schema diff detection in CI.

findings.title: No distributed tracing or structured logging
findings.description: No tracing (X-Ray, OpenTelemetry), no structured logging, no correlation IDs. Agent-initiated requests cannot be traced or debugged.
findings.gap: Complete absence of observability. Cannot trace agent-initiated requests.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK instrumentation and structured JSON logging with correlation IDs.

findings.title: No alerting on error rates or latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration. No CloudWatch alarms. No monitoring. Service degradation undetected until consumers report failures.
findings.gap: No alerting. No error rate or latency monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Deploy CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency with anomaly detection.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC exists. Manual infrastructure management. No peer review for infrastructure changes. No drift detection.
findings.gap: No IaC governance for agent-facing infrastructure surface.
findings.recommendation: Define infrastructure as code (Terraform/CDK) for API gateway, IAM, and network configuration.

findings.title: Plain string response format requires parsing
findings.description: Service returns plain strings ('ACCEPTED:<poNumber>' or 'ERROR:<message>') wrapped in SOAP envelope. No structured JSON.
findings.gap: String-based responses require custom parsing logic in agent tools.
findings.recommendation: Move to structured JSON responses when modernizing API.

findings.title: No identity propagation capability
findings.description: No identity propagation — no authentication exists. No JWT, no token exchange, no user context headers. Cannot distinguish agent-as-self from agent-on-behalf-of-partner.
findings.gap: No identity to propagate. Design for propagation when implementing auth.
findings.recommendation: Design auth with agent-as-self and agent-on-behalf-of-partner distinction from the start.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Manual Ant build with hand-run wsgen/wsimport. No automated testing or contract validation.
findings.gap: Cannot catch API breaking changes before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD with automated build, test, and API contract validation.

findings.title: No rollback capability
findings.description: No deployment infrastructure. Manual WAR deployment to JBoss. No blue/green, no canary, no automated rollback.
findings.gap: No automated rollback. Recovery depends on manual WAR redeployment.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green deployment with automated rollback triggers when containerizing.

findings.title: No sandbox/staging environment
findings.description: No environment configuration. Hardcoded production DB IP. No staging, sandbox, docker-compose, or seed data for testing.
findings.gap: Cannot test agents without risking production data.
findings.recommendation: Create containerized local environment with test database and seed data.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no evidence of operations >30s or long-running workflows.

evaluations.title: Event Emission for State Changes
evaluations.reason: Extended question — evaluated for stateful-crud but service has minimal complexity; single INSERT operation does not warrant event emission evaluation.

evaluations.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
evaluations.reason: Extended question — no rate limiting surface exists to document; STATE-Q5 covers the rate limiting gap.

evaluations.title: Concurrency Controls
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — though agent_scope is write-enabled and service has persistent state, the single INSERT without any concurrent-access pattern makes this redundant with API-Q4.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no P0 priority set, not identified as critical path.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — service has no list/query endpoints.

evaluations.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — though service has persistent state, no query endpoints exist to return temporal metadata.

evaluations.title: Data Quality Awareness
evaluations.reason: Extended question — no data quality tooling or metrics present; informational signal suppressed.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: Extended question — field names in WSDL and code are readable (partnerId, poNumber, amount); informational signal suppressed.

evaluations.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
evaluations.reason: Extended question — no data catalog or metadata layer; informational signal suppressed.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: Extended question — no metrics or telemetry of any kind; informational signal suppressed.

evaluations.title: API Test Coverage
evaluations.reason: Extended question — no tests exist at all; evaluated implicitly by ENG-Q2 finding (no CI/CD).

evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no IaC defines the data store; encryption config is not assessable from this repo alone.

items.summary: Resolve all 5 BLOCKERs and critical RISK-SAFETY findings. Focus on authentication, API modernization, idempotency, audit logging, and compensation logic.
Address remaining RISK-SAFETY (transaction limits, HITL) and RISK-QUALITY findings (error handling, observability, input validation, schema versioning).
Implement CI/CD, deployment automation, staging environment, and response format improvements.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy centralized identity and API gateway
recommended_actions.rationale: Authentication is the foundational blocker. API Gateway provides identity, scoped permissions, rate limiting, and agent suspension in a single deployment.

recommended_actions.action: Modernize API from SOAP to REST with OpenAPI
recommended_actions.rationale: SOAP cannot be consumed by agent frameworks. REST with OpenAPI enables automatic agent tool generation.
Write safety BLOCKERs — agents retry and may duplicate operations without idempotency. Cannot undo agent errors without compensation.

recommended_actions.action: Add structured audit logging with immutable storage
recommended_actions.rationale: Write operations must be auditable for compliance. Logging infrastructure enables both audit trails and operational observability.

recommended_actions.action: Remove hardcoded credentials and implement secrets management
recommended_actions.rationale: Credentials in source code are an immediate security vulnerability. Fastest RISK-SAFETY to remediate.

recommended_actions.action: Implement input validation and fix injection vulnerabilities
recommended_actions.rationale: XXE and SQL injection vulnerabilities are exploitable regardless of agent integration. Security fundamentals.
